source_text:
ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἀίδιός ἐστι, …
καὶ »Ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν« καὶ ὄνομα ἔοχεν αὐτὸ δὴ τοῦτο »Μεθ᾿ »ἡμῶν ὁ θεός« ὅτε δὲ ἐδημιούργησεν, ἐπεὶ μὴ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀποσταλεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς εἰς οὐσίαν ἔφερε τὰ πάντα, καὶ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἦν καὶ θεὸς ἦν· λέγεται δὲ καὶ σοφία ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱός, ἀρχὴ ὁδῶν τοῦ θεοῦ κτισθεῖσα κατὰ τὴν τῶν Παροιμιῶν γραφήν, ὅτι ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ σοφία, πρὸς τὸν οὗ ἐστι σοφία ὑπάρχουαα, οὐδεμίαν σχέοιν πρὸς ἕτερόν τινα εἶχεν, ἀλλ᾿ εὐδοκία θεοῦγενόμενος τὰ κτίοματα ὑπάρξαι ἠβονλήθη. ἠθέλησεν οὖν ἀναλαβεῖν αὕτη ἡ σοφία σχέσιν δημιουργικὴν πρὸς τὰ ἐσόμενα καὶ τοῦτό ἐστι τὸ δηλούμενον διὰ τοῦ ἐκτίσθαι αὐτὴν ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, καθ᾿ ἃς ὁδοὺς διαπορεύεται οὐσιῶν διακοσμῶν προνοούμενος, εὐεργετῶν, χαριζόμενος ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ σοφίᾳ κτισθείσῃ. ἀρχὴν οὖν εἶναι τὸν λόγον φασὶν οὐχ ἕτερον ὄντα αὐτῆς κατ᾿ οὐσίαν ἀλλ᾿ ἐπινοίᾳ καὶ σγέσει, ἵν᾿ ᾖ ἡ αὐτὴ ὕπαρξις ἣν νῦν καλοῦσιν κατ᾿ οὐσίαν αἱ γραφαί, ᾗ μὲν ᾠκείωται τῷ θεῷ σοφία, ᾗ δὲ νένευκεν, ἵν᾿ οὕτως εἴπω, πρὸς τὰ δημιουργήματα ὁ δημιονργικὸς λόγος, οὐκ ἐντανῦθα δὲ μόνον ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸς λόγος εἴρηται· ἔστι δὲ παραθέσθαι ἡητὰ οὐκ ἐκ τῆς καινῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐκ τῆς παλαιᾶς· »Τῷ λόγῳ γὰρ κυρίου οὐρανοὶ ἐστερεώθησαν«. καὶ τὸ »Ἀπέστειλεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰάσατο αὐτούς«.
thought_title: The Word as Wisdom and Creator
orientation: Origen is explaining why the Son is called both Word and Wisdom, and how the Word's relation to creation differs from his eternal relation to God.
pass_a_gloss: But since the Word of God is eternal, ... and "He tabernacled among us" and he had this very name "God with us." But when he created, since not as a man sent by the Father did he bring all things into being, he was both with God and was God. And the Son of God is also called Wisdom, created as the beginning of God's ways according to the scripture of Proverbs, because the Wisdom of God, existing toward him whose Wisdom she is, had no relation to any other, but having become by God's good pleasure he willed the creatures to exist. Therefore this Wisdom willed to take up a creative relation toward the things that were to be, and this is what is made clear through her having been created as the beginning of God's ways, along which ways he travels ordering beings, providing for them, doing good, granting gifts in this created Wisdom. Therefore they say that the Word is the beginning, not being other than her in substance but in conception and relation, so that the same existence may be which the scriptures now call according to substance, in that she is made at home with God as Wisdom, but in that she has inclined, so to speak, toward the creatures, the creative Word. And not only here is the Son of God called Word; it is possible to cite sayings not only from the New but also from the Old: "For by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm." And "He sent his word and healed them."

choices.why: Literal rendering of σκηνόω, preserving the dwelling/tent imagery of John 1:14
rejected: He pitched his tent among us

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for this key phrase from Proverbs
Literal rendering of σχέσις as relation, preserving Origen's technical distinction between substance and relation
Literal rendering preserving the philosophical distinction Origen draws between how the Word is conceived and his relational stance

choices.english: is made at home with God
choices.why: Literal rendering of οἰκειόω, preserving the sense of intimate belonging to God
Literal rendering of νεύω, preserving the spatial metaphor of leaning toward creatures

bible_refs.note: Τῷ λόγῳ γὰρ κυρίου οὐρανοὶ ἐστερεώθησαν
Ἀπέστειλεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰάσατο αὐτούς

pass_b_english: But the Word of God is eternal. And he tabernacled among us, and he received this very name, God with us. When he created, because he was not sent by the Father as a man, he brought all things into being. He was with God, and he was God.

The Son of God is also called Wisdom. According to the book of Proverbs, he was created as the beginning of God's ways. Why? Because the Wisdom of God, existing as the wisdom of the one whose wisdom it is, had no relation to anything else. But by God's good pleasure it willed that creatures should come into existence. This Wisdom therefore willed to take up a creative relation toward the things that were to be. This is what is made clear by its having been created as the beginning of God's ways. Along these ways he travels, ordering beings, providing, benefiting, and graciously giving, in this created Wisdom.

They say, then, that the Word is the beginning. He is not other than Wisdom in substance, but only in conception and relation. so that the same existence which the Scriptures now name as to substance is Wisdom insofar as it is at home with God, and the creative Word insofar as it has inclined, so to speak, toward the creatures.

Nor is the Son of God called Word only here. It is possible to cite passages not only from the New Testament but also from the Old: For by the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and He sent his word and healed them.
notes: The source text begins mid-sentence with ἀλλ᾿ ἐπεὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἀΐδιός ἐστι, followed by an ellipsis, indicating a gap in the preserved text.

OCR damage: ὑπάρχουαα should be ὑπάρχουσα (existing).
OCR damage: εὐδοκία θεοῦγενόμενος should likely be εὐδοκίᾳ θεοῦ γενόμενος (having become by God's good pleasure).

OCR damage: ἠβονλήθη should be ἠβουλήθη (he willed).

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and referents, smoothed the dense philosophical sentences into natural English, explained the Psalm numbering in the notes, and made the relationship between Wisdom and Word clearer without altering any claims.

notes.quote: created as the beginning of God's ways

variants.text: created as the beginning of God's ways
the beginning, not being other than Wisdom
inclined, so to speak, toward the creatures

notes.why: Four different descriptions of Wisdom/Word's relation to creation without explaining they are synonymous metaphors.
notes.fix: Add note: all describe same eternal Word's voluntary creative act.

notes.why: Wisdom, Word, and 'excellence' are treated as interchangeable but reader may not grasp this.
notes.fix: Note: 'excellence' translates same Greek term as Wisdom/Word.

notes.why: Modern Bibles number this Psalm 33:6; 'LXX' unexplained.
notes.fix: Add: 'LXX=Septuagint, Greek Bible; numbered Psalm 33 in Hebrew.'

notes.why: Modern Bibles number this Psalm 107:20; 'LXX' unexplained.

notes.quote: the Wisdom of God, existing as the wisdom of the one whose wisdom it is, had no relation to anything else
notes.why: Circular and opaque; 'wisdom of the one whose wisdom it is' is tautological gloss.
notes.fix: Revise: 'the Wisdom of God, belonging properly to God alone, had no external relation'

notes.quote: this is what is made clear by its having been created as the beginning of God's ways, along which ways it travels
notes.why: Antecedent of 'its' unclear; 'created' contradicts eternal Word; 'travels' is bizarre metaphor.
notes.fix: Note: 'created' here means 'appointed/constituted,' not made from nothing; 'travels' means 'extends care'

notes.quote: created as the beginning of God's ways
notes.why: 'Created' applied to eternal Wisdom contradicts Origen's entire argument; likely translates 'established' or 'constituted.'
notes.fix: Translate 'constituted' or 'appointed' to avoid implying creatureliness

notes.why: Unusual English rendering of John 1:14; reader may not recognize it.
notes.fix: Use standard 'dwelt among us' or gloss the term.

notes.quote: They say, then, that the Word is the beginning
notes.why: Unclear who 'they' are—Origen's own school, opponents, or another tradition.
notes.fix: Identify whose view is being reported.

notes.quote: he was both with God and was God
notes.why: Confusing syntax; 'was not sent…as a man' clashes with pre-incarnation creation context.
notes.fix: Rephrase to clarify the temporal logic.

notes.quote: the same existence which the Scriptures now call by substance is Wisdom insofar as it is made at home with God
notes.why: Dense philosophical sentence reads like word-for-word gloss; hard to follow as English.
notes.fix: Rewrite for clarity, unpacking the substance/relation distinction.

notes.quote: He sent his word and healed them
notes.why: Psalm 106:20 LXX reads 'He sent his word and healed them' but standard English Bibles have Psalm 107:20; numbering may confuse.
notes.fix: Clarify LXX vs. Hebrew numbering difference for Psalm citations.

last_rejected.why: The Greek states the Wisdom willed the creatures to exist; the English adds 'by God's good pleasure' which is not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: but it willed that creatures should come into existence
last_rejected.ruling: Greek includes εὐδοκία θεοῦ (‘God’s good pleasure’), so translation matches source.

last_rejected.quote: ordering, providing for, benefiting, and graciously giving to all things in this created Wisdom
last_rejected.source_quote: διαπορεύεται οὐσιῶν διακοσμῶν προνοούμενος, εὐεργετῶν, χαριζόμενος ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ σοφίᾳ κτισθείσῃ
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'ordering substances' (οὐσιῶν), not 'all things'; 'all things' is an addition not supported by the text.
last_rejected.fix: ordering substances, providing for, benefiting, and graciously giving in this created Wisdom
last_rejected.ruling: Greek says διαπορεύεται οὐσιῶν …, i.e., moves through substances; ‘ordering … all things’ adds unsupported nuance.

problems.quote: Along these ways it travels, ordering all things, providing for them, benefiting them, and graciously giving to them in this created Wisdom.
problems.source_quote: καθ᾿ ἃς ὁδοὺς διαπορεύεται οὐσιῶν διακοσμῶν προνοούμενος, εὐεργετῶν, χαριζόμενος ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ σοφίᾳ κτισθείσῃ
problems.why: The masculine participles mark someone acting in the created Wisdom, not Wisdom traveling and giving.
problems.fix: Along these ways he travels, ordering beings, providing, benefiting, and graciously giving, in this created Wisdom.
problems.ruling: διαπορεύεται οὐσιῶν διακοσμῶν προνοούμενος, εὐεργετῶν, χαριζόμενος are masculine, so the Logos travels and acts 'in this created Wisdom'; English makes Wisdom the subject.

problems.quote: The same existence which the Scriptures now call by substance is Wisdom insofar as it is made at home with God
problems.source_quote: ἵν᾿ ᾖ ἡ αὐτὴ ὕπαρξις ἣν νῦν καλοῦσιν κατ᾿ οὐσίαν αἱ γραφαί
problems.why: A purpose clause, so that it be the same existence, is turned into a bare assertion.
problems.fix: so that the same existence which the Scriptures now name as to substance is Wisdom insofar as it is at home with God
problems.ruling: ἵν᾿ ᾖ ἡ αὐτὴ ὕπαρξις is a purpose clause ('so that it be the same existence'); English drops the ἵνα and asserts it flatly.

edits.old: Along these ways it travels, ordering all things, providing for them, benefiting them, and graciously giving to them in this created Wisdom.
edits.new: Along these ways he travels, ordering beings, providing, benefiting, and graciously giving, in this created Wisdom.

edits.old: The same existence which the Scriptures now call by substance is Wisdom insofar as it is made at home with God
edits.new: so that the same existence which the Scriptures now name as to substance is Wisdom insofar as it is at home with God

fixed: Agency corrected: masculine participles (διαπορεύεται, διακοσμῶν, προνοούμενος, εὐεργετῶν, χαριζόμενος) refer to the Son/Word acting in the created Wisdom, not Wisdom herself traveling and giving.
Modality corrected: 'ἵν᾿ ᾖ' is a purpose clause ('so that it be'), not a declarative statement. English now reflects the subjunctive purpose.

problems.quote: When he created, he was not sent by the Father as a man to bring all things into being.
problems.source_quote: ὅτε δὲ ἐδημιούργησεν, ἐπεὶ μὴ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀποσταλεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς εἰς οὐσίαν ἔφερε τὰ πάντα
problems.why: μὴ negates only 'sent as a man.' He did bring all things into being; English makes that an unfulfilled purpose.
problems.fix: When he created, because he was not sent by the Father as a man, he brought all things into being.
problems.ruling: μὴ negates only 'ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀποσταλεὶς'; ἔφερε τὰ πάντα states he did bring all things into being. English 'was not sent... to bring' implies purpose unfulfilled, misleading.

edits.old: When he created, he was not sent by the Father as a man to bring all things into being.
edits.new: When he created, because he was not sent by the Father as a man, he brought all things into being.

fixed: Fixed negation scope: μὴ negates only 'sent as a man' (ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀποσταλεὶς); the source says he did bring all things into being (εἰς οὐσίαν ἔφερε τὰ πάντα).

last_rejected.quote: When he created, because he was not sent by the Father as a man, he brought all things into being. He was with God, and he was God.
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅτε δὲ ἐδημιούργησεν, ἐπεὶ μὴ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἀποσταλεὶς ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς εἰς οὐσίαν ἔφερε τὰ πάντα, καὶ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἦν καὶ θεὸς ἦν
last_rejected.why: The English gets the logic backwards. In the Greek, 'he was with God and was God' is the main claim. It holds because he did not create as a man sent by the Father. Creating is not the result of not being sent.
last_rejected.fix: But when he created, since it was not as a man sent by the Father that he brought all things into being, he was 'with God' and 'was God.'
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἐπεὶ μὴ… directly precedes ἔφερε τὰ πάντα; English causal matches. καὶ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἦν καὶ θεὸς ἦν is still stated.
